title: SkinVision app rated a changing mole on Jason Sheridan's arm high risk; a dermatologist found stage 1A melanoma and it was removed
summary: SkinVision rated a 31-year-old's changing arm mole high risk; stage 1A melanoma was found and removed, and he is cancer-free.
account: Jason Sheridan, a 31-year-old office worker from Liverpool living in Vauxhall, South London, noticed a new 1cm mole on his left arm in March 2018. He did not see a doctor. Twelve months later it turned pink and he checked it with SkinVision, an AI app that grades photographed moles low, medium or high risk. It returned a high-risk rating and urged him to see a doctor. His GP referred him to a dermatologist and two weeks later the mole was removed in a 40-minute operation. The biopsy showed stage 1A melanoma, a further biopsy found no spread, and he is cancer-free. The Daily Mail reported the case on 17 January 2020 without dates for the app check or surgery.
purpose: SkinVision is built to grade a phone photograph of a mole low, medium or high risk. It tells users with a high-risk result to see a doctor, with dermatologist advice sent within 48 hours. This benefit is that intended use.
system: SkinVision skin-check app (AI analysis of smartphone photographs of moles, graded low, medium or high risk)

ratings.reason: A biopsy-confirmed stage 1A melanoma was excised, further tests found no spread and he is reported cancer-free. He calls it life-saving, but stage 1A is early disease and no clinician is quoted on prognosis. How long he would otherwise have waited is his own estimate.

ai_role.statement: The app's classifier graded a phone photograph of the mole high risk and told him to see a doctor at once. By his account that prompt, not the color change, is what sent him to his GP. He said he only goes to the doctor when absolutely desperate. The referral, excision, biopsy and staging were done by the GP, the dermatologist and pathology, none of whom the Daily Mail quotes. The article does not report the app's score, its version, or whether the 48-hour dermatologist advice it mentions was used.

evidence.citation: Howard H (2020). Saved by an app: Office worker, 31, is diagnosed with a deadly form of skin cancer after his mobile phone warned him about a tiny mole on his arm. Daily Mail, 17 January 2020.
